Private information: facedown card fronts, discard fronts, world-deck count, and world-deck backs below the top. Public: discard counts/backs, board resource/warband counts, and everything else. A holder may inspect and show facedown advisers to others; identity may be discussed or lied about.
Component limits

Read rules literally: Law overrides Playbook/aids except Site Reference; nonitalic rules override italic reminders. “Must” overrides ordinary rules, “cannot” overrides even “must,” and “ignore” overrides named must/cannot restrictions. “Must if able” has no penalty if unable. Give and Take are distinct keywords; restricting one does not restrict the other.
Rules priority

Ordinary promises are nonbinding; pieces cannot be transferred without a rule permitting it. Exceptions include Citizenship offers and expressly binding powers/deals (including Tribunal’s permitted binding arrangements). Tribunal allows binding immediate favor/secret exchanges and binding future actions with agreed penalties, not unrestricted immediate relic/banner transfers; disputed breach is settled by coin flip. Reliquary relics are not tradable by other binding-deal powers.

When uncovered, Chancellor must apply the modifier: Brutal makes the defeated player kill their entire force when Chancellor attacks, even if Chancellor loses; Decadent makes Provinces/Hinterland→Cradle Travel free but Travel to Hinterland +1; Careless adds 1 favor to every Trade (even secret trades) but gives 1 fewer secret on secret trades; Greedy Search draws 2 extra cards (still stops at world Vision) but prohibits Search costing over 2 Supply.

Only an Imperial Chronicle winner may build or repair one edifice. At a ruled site with no intact or ruined edifice, replace a denizen with matching intact Archive edifice and return denizen to world deck; or flip a ruled ruin intact. A site already holding a ruin is not eligible for building a new edifice, since it does not meet “no intact or ruined edifice.”

Discard every site except one the winner rules or one with an intact edifice; shuffle discarded sites into site deck, discard their denizens, return their relics to relic deck, and ruined edifices to Archive. At retained sites the winner does not rule, flip any intact edifice to ruin and discard all denizens there. Set aside every site with ruins, attached ruins, remaining denizens, relics in map order.

Repack in order: excluding set-aside ruins, fill Cradle top-down by pushing Cradle sites up then importing Provinces then Hinterland top-down. Fill Provinces top-down by pushing up then importing Hinterland top-down. Push Hinterland sites up. Fill empty Hinterland slots bottom-up with set-aside ruins bottom-up; then do empty Provinces slots similarly. Fill remaining spaces with facedown site-deck cards; in each region with no faceup site, flip its top site faceup.

Yes. Homeland reward triggers when a matching-suit card is played there unless you discarded a card of that same suit at that site this turn; discarding a different suit does not suppress it. Printed reward may be a shared-bank secret, favor from matching bank, 2 warbands, or its relic treated as Recover. Resolve normal site-play favor, then Homeland reward, then When Played effect. Taking a relic this way costs no Supply or ordinary site resource cost.
Site powers (Site Reference)

given_state: A matching-suit card is played to a Homeland after a different-suit discard at that site this turn.
completed_events: The different-suit card was discarded at that same site this turn; matching card is now played there.
next_operation: Check whether a same-suit discard suppressed the Homeland reward, then resolve site favor, reward, When Played in order.
result: The different-suit discard does not suppress reward. If relic reward, take it as Recover with no Supply or site resource cost.

Traveling from one Coast to another costs 1 Supply and ignores Narrow Pass. A Coast only as destination does not suffice; both origin and destination must be Coast sites.
Site powers (Site Reference)

Narrow Pass requires entry to its site when entering its region from another region. Targeting anything in its region from another region also requires targeting Narrow Pass unless you rule it. Ruling Narrow Pass waives both requirements.
Site powers (Site Reference)

To travel to Hidden Place or declare Campaign targets there, flip 1 secret on your board facedown. Only an effect that explicitly ignores Hidden Place can override that restriction; a general no-Supply effect does not. Buried Giant’s listed power ignores Narrow Pass, not Hidden Place.

From Buried Giant, flip 1 of your board secrets facedown to spend no Supply and ignore Narrow Pass. This expressly ignores Narrow Pass, not Hidden Place; Hidden Place still needs its own facedown secret unless another power ignores it. The secret stays facedown/exhausted and cannot pay another cost until readied.
